chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Marwan, from Abu Khudayrah, from one who heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) say:

He mentioned the martyrs. He said: Some of us said, 'In the one with a stomach ail (dying of dysentery).' Some of us said, 'In the one whose body is eaten by beasts.' Some of us said, 'Other than that, from what is mentioned regarding martyrdom.' Then a man said, 'I did not think that the martyr was only one who was killed in the cause of Allah.'
So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said, 'Then the martyrs would surely be few.'
"Those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are [in the ranks of] the righteous and the martyrs, in the sight of their Lord."
Then he said, 'This is for us and for our Shias.'
ai.seo_question: Who qualifies as a martyr in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) broadens the concept of martyrdom beyond battlefield deaths to include those who perish from natural causes like stomach ailments or being devoured by beasts, arguing that if only combat deaths counted, the number of martyrs would be too small. He cites the verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah to link this expanded definition of 'Shuhada' to the Ahl al-Bayt and their Shias, establishing a unique spiritual status for their followers that transcends physical death in war.
